facts.text: Do not use if the patient is allergic to omeprazole; severe skin reactions such as reddening, blisters, or rash may occur.
Omeprazole is not indicated for children under 18 years; a doctor should be consulted before use.

Seek immediate medical attention if experiencing difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black/tarry stools, light‑headedness, chest or shoulder pain, shortness of breath, or persistent wheezing with heartburn.
Persistent heartburn lasting more than 3 months, unexplained weight loss, nausea/vomiting, or stomach pain may signal a serious condition; consult a doctor.

If heartburn continues or worsens, treatment exceeds 14 days, more than one 14‑day course is needed within 4 months, diarrhea develops, or a rash/joint pain appears, stop the product and contact a healthcare professional.
Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a health professional before using omeprazole.
Keep the product out of reach of children.
In case of overdose, obtain medical help or contact a Poison Control Center (1‑800‑222‑1222) immediately.
Acid‑reducing agents, including omeprazole, may interact with certain prescription drugs; patients should ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if they are taking prescription medications.

Adults (≥18 years) should swallow 1 tablet with a glass of water before breakfast, once daily, for a 14‑day course; do not exceed 1 tablet per day or use longer than 14 days unless directed by a physician.
Tablets must be swallowed whole; do not chew or crush.
A 14‑day course may be repeated no more frequently than every 4 months, unless a doctor advises otherwise.
